featuredStory.title: SEBI Formalizes SM REIT Framework: Opening ₹5 Lakh Crore Fractional Asset Pipeline
featuredStory.excerpt: SEBI's landmark framework for Small and Medium REITs brings commercial, warehousing, and industrial micro-assets under institutional trustee oversight with a ₹10 Lakh minimum investment threshold.
featuredStory.analysisSummary: By establishing a dedicated migration pathway for unlisted fractional real estate SPVs into SEBI-regulated SM REITs, the regulator has eliminated opaque private structures, enforced 95% net distributable cash flow pass-through, and created exchange-listed secondary liquidity.

quickQueries.query: What is the new SEBI SM REIT limit?
quickQueries.response: Under SEBI's March 2024 regulations, Small and Medium REITs (SM REITs) cover commercial or industrial asset portfolios with an aggregate asset value between ₹50 Crores and ₹500 Crores. The statutory minimum ticket size for retail investors is set at ₹10 Lakhs, and the trust must distribute at least 95% of Net Distributable Cash Flows.

quickQueries.query: How are InvIT distributions taxed in FY 2025-26?
quickQueries.response: InvIT cash distributions are multi-component. Under current Indian Finance Act provisions: (1) Dividend income is typically tax-exempt if the SPV has not opted for concessional corporate tax; (2) Interest income is taxable at your marginal income slab; (3) Return of Capital (RoC) distributions are tax-deferred, reducing your asset acquisition cost basis until cost reaches zero, after which it is taxed as capital gains.
keyPoints: Dividend: Tax-exempt or taxed at slab depending on SPV regime
Interest: Taxed at investor marginal slab
Return of Capital: Deferred capital gains adjustment
TDS: Applicable on interest component above statutory threshold

quickQueries.query: Difference between AIF Cat II and PMS?
quickQueries.response: Portfolio Management Services (PMS) manage individual segregated demat accounts directly in your name with a statutory minimum entry of ₹50 Lakhs, predominantly trading listed equities. Category II Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) are pooled, close-ended trusts with a ₹1 Crore minimum entry that invest in unlisted equity, private credit, and pre-IPO instruments with statutory tax pass-through status under Section 115UB.
keyPoints: Minimum Entry: PMS ₹50 Lakhs vs. AIF ₹1 Crore
Structure: Segregated individual account (PMS) vs. Pooled close-ended trust (AIF)
Asset Focus: Listed equities (PMS) vs. Private debt & unlisted assets (AIF Cat II)
Tax Status: Direct capital gains (PMS) vs. Section 115UB pass-through (AIF)

quickQueries.query: What is NDCF (Net Distributable Cash Flow)?
quickQueries.response: Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) is the statutory metric governed by SEBI representing the actual cash available for distribution to unit-holders after deducting property operating expenses, debt service interest, and routine maintenance capital expenditure from gross rental or tariff collections. SEBI mandates that Indian REITs and InvITs distribute at least 90% of their NDCF.
keyPoints: Cash, not accounting profit: Excludes non-cash depreciation and fair value adjustments
Statutory 90% payout rule enforced by SEBI
Calculated at both SPV level and Trust holding level
Guarantees that rental collections flow directly to unit-holders
